result.text:
Great post!

Short sellers spent months calling $FIGR’s blockchain infrastructure "just PR."  

Meanwhile, Bank of America ($BAC) just onboarded as a DART participant.  

Why this actually matters for the P&L: 

1. Removes warehouse friction: Originators and loan buyers with BofA warehouse lines can now finance and move assets on Figure’s rails without legacy MERS bottlenecks. 

2. Validates the plumbing: DART jumped from 2% adoption in 2024 to 87% across Figure ecosystem loans, and direct participation from a Tier-1 bank provides third-party institutional validation that legacy short reports claimed would never happen.

3. Feeds Figure Connect: Smoother institutional warehouse financing directly unlocks higher capital-light marketplace throughput.  

Wall Street still prices $FIGR like a cyclical balance-sheet lender while Tier-1 banks integrate into its settlement infrastructure. And @MBTannenbaum teasing "more to come for this partnership" heading into 2027 is the real signal.

result.text:
Bank of America has joined the Figure platform and become a DART (Digital Asset Registry Technology) Participant. Over the years, current and prospective originators and investors have inquired about using Bank of America as their warehouse provider. Now, ecosystem participants can work with America directly and discuss the extension of their existing credit facilities (or the establishment of new ones) for the financing of assets on the Figure platform. 

Bank of America is one of the largest banks in the country and bringing an institution like this is a major feat. 

More to come for this partnership.

$FIGR This is a major strategic win for Figure, as $BAC becomes partnered with Figure as a DART participant, potentially removing a major obstacle for originators and investors who want to use Figure while maintaining their existing warehouse financing relationships with BofA.

DART is Figure's blockchain-based alternative to MERS, the traditional mortgage registry. It tracks loan ownership and interests, enabling automated updates as loans change hands. The underlying infrastructure has applications across additional loan types, and Figure's 10-K document noted that DART adoption was 87% across Figure ecosystem loans (from just 2% in 2024).

What's most interesting to me is what this could signify for Figure's future. Adding one of America's largest banks validates the infrastructure and advantages of DART vs MERS, likely accelerates institutional adoption, and opens the door to greater financing activity on Figure Connect. 

This agreement also underscores what has become a reality: Figure is a platform, with 72% of their income derived from the ecosystem and platform, not their own loans. DART is just one of many parts of their technology flywheel which is accelerating into 2027's, "Year of the Upsell."

@MBTannenbaum's "More to come for this partnership," is particularly intriguing.

Nvidia sold large volumes of advanced AI chips billed through Singapore companies. The vast majority never stayed in Singapore (reports cite figures well above 90% shipped or accessed elsewhere). U.S. authorities have investigated diversion and remote-access arrangements that likely sent the chips’ computing power to China, undermining export controls meant to protect American security and technological edge. New rules are now closing those loopholes. 
The pattern is clear: short-term corporate gains, long-term costs and risks shifted onto ordinary Americans.
